Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are the special case of preparations in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation; general composite preparations are linear combinations and mixtures and need not factor. A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

**(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

**(a) State space.** Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] for a declared system of the declared massive-matter sector, with its assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$. The **state space of the system in the model** is the set
$$D(H)=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}$$
of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]: the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators on $H$ of trace one. A **state** of the system is an element of $D(H)$; this is the geometry vocabulary for the general preparations of clause (iii) of the state postulate. The model's adopted assignment of a state to each preparation is not produced by this definition; it is the content of that postulate.

**(b) Pure and mixed states.** A state is **pure** when it is one of the operators $T_{u,u}$ with $u\in S(H)$, and **mixed** when it is not pure, as in [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the map
$$j:R(H)\to D(H),\qquad j([\psi])=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
is a bijection of the ray space onto the set of pure states; and by clause (ii) of the state postulate the pure preparations are the unit rays of $H$, so the model's pure preparations are exactly its pure states.

**(c) State assigned to a state vector.** For a nonzero vector $\psi\in H^{\times}$ the **state assigned to $\psi$** is the normalized rank-one operator
$$\widehat\rho(\psi)=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}\in D(H),$$
which by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] depends only on the ray $[\psi]$; clause (ii) of the state postulate assigns the same operator to the pure preparation $[\psi]$. The zero vector is excluded here because $\|\psi\|^{-1}$ is defined only for $\psi\ne0$; no state is assigned to it, in agreement with the state postulate.

**(d) Mixtures and purity.** A **statistical mixture** of preparations with weights is the trace-norm convergent sum of clause (iii) of the state postulate; its value is the corresponding convex combination of states. The **purity** of a state $\rho$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})$, and by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-purity-criterion]] a state is pure exactly when its purity equals $1$.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) record the readings of the state postulate in the geometry vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. The cited mathematical suppliers of the ray-to-state correspondence and of the purity criterion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is carried as a hypothesis of these readings. They adopt no assumption beyond the state postulate and that hypothesis, assert no dynamics, no probability law and no measurement model, and make no empirical claim: in particular, whether a given laboratory preparation is pure or mixed, and whether a given apparatus realizes a prescribed mixture, are physical identifications with uncertainty, governed by the preparation and apparatus assumptions of the framework, not consequences of this definition. Superselection restrictions and identical-particle symmetry sectors, where imposed, are separate assumptions by clause (v) of the state postulate and are not part of the state space fixed here.
For every real $\theta$, $\exp(i\theta)=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$.

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(-x)=-\sin x,\qquad\cos(-x)=\cos x,\qquad\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1.$$
Consequently $|\sin x|\le1$ and $|\cos x|\le1$.

Let $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$ be measurable and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$
for every $x$. Then
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] (P5) for a spinless particle of mass $m>0$ and action constant $\hbar>0$, with state space $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ as in [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]), and for a unit vector $\psi\in H$ let $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}$ and $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}$ be the outcome laws of the assigned observables $Q_{j}$ and $P_{j}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Then:

(a) **Position observable.** $Q_{j}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(Q_{j})=\{\psi\in H:x_{j}\psi\in H\}$, its spectral PVM is given by $E_{Q_{j}}(B)\psi=\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\psi$, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}).$$
The law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure with density
$$f_{j}(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi(x_{\perp},t)|^{2}\,dx_{\perp},$$
the $j$-th marginal density of $|\psi|^{2}$, and it is atomless: $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Moreover $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$.

(b) **Joint position law.** There is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}\subseteq\mathbb R$, and its scalar law in the preparation $\psi$ is the measure of the density $|\psi|^{2}$:
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}\ \text{Borel}).$$
For a density-operator preparation $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, its joint scalar law is
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B))=\sum_nw_n\int_B|u_n(x)|^{2}\,dx=\int_Bf_{\rho}(x)\,dx,\qquad f_{\rho}(x):=\sum_nw_n|u_n(x)|^{2},$$
where $f_{\rho}\in L^{1}(\mathbb R^{3})$ is a nonnegative density class of total integral $1$, by [F8] and Tonelli. Thus the model's joint position law in a spatial region $B$ has density $|\psi|^{2}$ for a pure preparation and $f_{\rho}$ for a density-operator preparation.

(c) **Momentum observable.** $P_{j}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(P_{j})=\{\psi\in H:\xi_{j}\mathcal F_{2}\psi\in L^{2}\}$ and Fourier representation $\mathcal F_{2}(P_{j}\psi)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{j}\,\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)$; its spectral PVM is $E_{P_{j}}(B)=\mathcal F_{2}^{-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}\mathcal F_{2}$ with $m(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}$, and
$$\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)|^{2}\,d\xi,\qquad m^{-1}(B)=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^{3}:2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}\in B\}.$$
The law is absolutely continuous with density
$$g_{j}(p)=\frac{1}{2\pi\hbar}\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}\bigl|\mathcal F_{2}\psi\bigl(\xi_{\perp},\tfrac{p}{2\pi\hbar}\bigr)\bigr|^{2}d\xi_{\perp}$$
in the momentum variable $p$, and it is atomless; moreover $\sigma(P_{j})=\mathbb R$.

(d) **Exact values.** For every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ one has $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ and $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every preparation, although both observables have spectrum $\mathbb R$: an exact position or momentum value is not an outcome of the model's sharp law, while its finite-resolution readings are the Borel bin probabilities of (a)-(c).

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, on the massive spinless model of P5 and on the cited mathematics. The componentwise extension to the spin-$s$ model is not proved here; no joint statistics of a position and a momentum observable, no dynamics and no apparatus or empirical claim are made. The identification of the operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ with concrete laboratory position and momentum measurements is a tested identification under P7 and is not asserted by this item.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $E_{A,x}(B):=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ be its scalar measures ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ say that $\lambda$ is an **eigenvalue** of $A$ when $Ax=\lambda x$ for some nonzero $x\in D(A)$, the domain-restricted reading of [[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]. Then:

(a) The orthogonal projection $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection of $H$ onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)=\{x\in D(A):Ax=\lambda x\}$; in particular $E_A(\{\lambda\})\ne0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$.

(b) For every density operator $\rho$ on $H$, that is every self-adjoint positive trace-class $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)), the number $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(\{\lambda\}))$ is the weight that the scalar law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ assigns to the singleton $\{\lambda\}$: it vanishes for every $\rho$ whenever $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$, and it equals $1$ for the pure state $T_{u,u}$ of every unit eigenvector $u\in\ker(A-\lambda)$.

(c) If $A$ has no eigenvalues at all, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every density operator $\rho$ and every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$: the scalar law of every state carries no point mass, while its values on general Borel sets remain $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$.

Clauses (a)-(c) are mathematical statements about $A$, $E_A$ and the density operators; no physical interpretation of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is asserted here.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

derivations.claim: [The plane wave is not in the state space] By [F2], $|\psi_{k}(x)|^{2}=1$ for every $x$ and $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|\psi_{k}|^{2}dx=+\infty$; hence $\psi_{k}\notin H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$. For every nonzero scalar $z$ the same computation gives $\int|z\psi_{k}|^{2}=|z|^{2}\cdot\infty=\infty$, so no nonzero scalar multiple of $\psi_{k}$ lies in $H$ either, and the formal normalization "$\psi_{k}/\sqrt{V}$" depends on a box volume $V$ and is also not an element of $H$.

[The exact-position symbol is not a state] Suppose $x\in H$ were an eigenvector of $Q_{j}$ at some $\lambda$, that is $Q_{j}x=\lambda x$ with $x\ne0$; then $\lambda$ would be an eigenvalue of $Q_{j}$. But [F3] states that $Q_{j}$ has no eigenvalues, and its law is atomless, so no such $x$ exists. The symbol $\delta^{3}(x-X)$ is not a function class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and cannot be an eigenvector; the model's corresponding exact-position statement is instead $\mu^{Q_{j}}(\{X\})=0$ for every preparation.

[Hence no preparation is assigned to either object] By [F1] pure preparations are unit rays of $H$ and general preparations are density operators on $H$; since neither $\psi_{k}$ nor $\delta^{3}(x-X)$ determines an element of $H$, neither determines a preparation, and no position density can be attached to them within the model. The identities $|\psi_{k}|^{2}=1$ and "$\delta$ is localized" are formal statements outside the state space, not probabilities of the model.

[The pointwise solution property does not supply a state] Granting that the free plane wave satisfies $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi_{k}=E\psi_{k}$ pointwise with $E=\hbar^{2}|k|^{2}/(2m)$, and that the time-dependent expression $e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}$ with $\omega=E/\hbar$ solves the free Schrödinger equation classically, those are statements about a smooth function on $\mathbb R^{3}$ and do not place it in $H$; the model's dynamics and its Born law are defined on the state space, and by steps 1.1-2.1 the plane wave is not in it. The finite-resolution content of the model is the bin probability of a normalizable packet, not the idealized plane wave. Specifically, under the stated hypotheses of [[ex-nrqm-observables-position-bin-probabilities]] clauses (i)-(ii), for its Gaussian first-coordinate packet, every bin $(a,b]$ with $a<b$ has positive probability, whereas every exact first-coordinate value has probability zero. Positivity in every positive-length bin is not claimed for arbitrary normalizable packets. This refutes the displayed claim.

boundaries.reason: The state space is nonzero and the refuted objects are specific nonzero formal expressions; no empty case arises.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 shows no nonzero scalar multiple of the plane wave lies in the state space, and step 2.1 that no preparation is assigned to it.
Step 1.2 treats the exact-value singleton and the constant modulus one of the plane wave.

boundaries.reason: No eigenvalue or multiplicity claim is made; the position observable has no eigenvalues and its law is atomless.
No interval endpoints enter; the argument concerns membership in L^2 and singleton outcome sets.

boundaries.evidence: The statement assumes Countable Choice for the L^2 and convergence facts used in steps 1.1-2.1.
Step 1.1 proves that constant modulus one forces divergence of the squared-norm integral, so the object is not in L^2.
Step 2.1 proves that an object outside L^2 determines no preparation, the converse direction of the assignment rule.

(d) **Exact values.** For every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ one has $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ and $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every preparation, although both observables have spectrum $\mathbb R$: an exact position or momentum value is not an outcome of the model's sharp law, while its finite-resolution readings are the Borel bin probabilities of (a)-(c).

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, on the massive spinless model of P5 and on the cited mathematics. The componentwise extension to the spin-$s$ model is not proved here; no joint statistics of a position and a momentum observable, no dynamics and no apparatus or empirical claim are made. **(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

derivations.claim: [Normalization of the Gaussian packet] With $c=\sigma^{2}$ in [F1], $\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-t^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}dt=\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}$. Therefore $\int_{\mathbb R}|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}dt=(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}=1$, since $|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}=(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-t^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}$ by [F4]; consequently $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|\psi|^{2}dx=\left(\int_{\mathbb R}|\psi_{\sigma}|^{2}\right)\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\varphi|^{2}\right)=1$ by Tonelli [F3], so $\psi$ is a unit vector and $[\psi]$ is a pure preparation of the model by [F5].

[The position law and its density] By [F2] the law of $Q_{1}$ in the preparation $[\psi]$ is $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{1}^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}dx$; writing the integrand as $|\psi_{\sigma}(x_{1})|^{2}|\varphi(x_{2},x_{3})|^{2}$ by [F4] and iterating the integral by Tonelli [F3], $\int_{x_{1}^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}dx=\left(\int_{B}|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}dt\right)\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\varphi|^{2}\right)=\int_{B}|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}dt$, which is clause (i) with density $f_{1}(t)=|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}$.

[Exact values and bin bounds] By [F2] (the atomless clause of the position law) $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every $\lambda$, so no exact coordinate value carries probability. For any finite $a<b$, put $M:=\max\{|a|,|b|\}$. Every $t\in[a,b]$ satisfies $|t|\le M$, and therefore [given, step 2.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra]
$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}}e^{-M^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}\le|\psi_{\sigma}(t)|^{2}\le\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}}.$$
Integrating these inequalities over $(a,b]$ and using the position law in [F2] and monotonicity [F3] gives the two displayed bounds. Their lower bound is strictly positive because $a<b$ and $\sigma>0$, so every bin of positive length receives positive probability, including bins crossing the origin and bins with negative endpoints. For the symmetric bin $(-\sigma,\sigma]$, the substitution $u=t/\sigma$ in step 2.1 gives $\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}((-\sigma,\sigma])=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-1}^{1}e^{-u^{2}/2}du$, and since $e^{-1/2}\le e^{-u^{2}/2}\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, monotonicity [F3] yields $\sqrt{2/(\pi e)}\le\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}((-\sigma,\sigma])\le\sqrt{2/\pi}$. The final upper bound for $(-\delta,\delta]$ is the general upper estimate with $a=-\delta$, $b=\delta$; its lower estimate is positive for every $\delta>0$.

Let $(a_k)$ be a sequence of reals with $a_k \ge 0$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$,
let $s_n = \sum_{k<n} a_k$ be its partial sums and let
$S = \{\, s_n : n \in \mathbb{N} \,\}$ be the range of $(s_n)$ ([[def-series]]).
Then:

1. $(s_n)$ is nondecreasing ([[def-monotone-sequence]]) and $s_n \ge 0$ for every
   $n$;
2. $\sum a_k$ converges **if and only if** $S$ is bounded above
   ([[def-bounded-set]]), and in that case
   $$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k \;=\; \sup S ,$$
   so in particular $s_n \le \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k$ for every $n$;
3. if $S$ is not bounded above then $s_n \to +\infty$
   ([[def-divergence-to-infinity]]) and $\sum a_k$ diverges.

This is the theorem that makes the nonnegative theory work: for terms of one
sign, convergence is a boundedness question and no candidate limit is ever
needed. Every comparison test on this page is an application of it.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] (P5) for a spinless particle of mass $m>0$ and action constant $\hbar>0$, with state space $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ as in [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]), and for a unit vector $\psi\in H$ let $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}$ and $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}$ be the outcome laws of the assigned observables $Q_{j}$ and $P_{j}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Then:

(a) **Position observable.** $Q_{j}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(Q_{j})=\{\psi\in H:x_{j}\psi\in H\}$, its spectral PVM is given by $E_{Q_{j}}(B)\psi=\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\psi$, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}).$$
The law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure with density
$$f_{j}(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi(x_{\perp},t)|^{2}\,dx_{\perp},$$
the $j$-th marginal density of $|\psi|^{2}$, and it is atomless: $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Moreover $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$.

(b) **Joint position law.** There is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}\subseteq\mathbb R$, and its scalar law in the preparation $\psi$ is the measure of the density $|\psi|^{2}$:
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}\ \text{Borel}).$$
For a density-operator preparation $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, its joint scalar law is
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B))=\sum_nw_n\int_B|u_n(x)|^{2}\,dx=\int_Bf_{\rho}(x)\,dx,\qquad f_{\rho}(x):=\sum_nw_n|u_n(x)|^{2},$$
where $f_{\rho}\in L^{1}(\mathbb R^{3})$ is a nonnegative density class of total integral $1$, by [F8] and Tonelli. Thus the model's joint position law in a spatial region $B$ has density $|\psi|^{2}$ for a pure preparation and $f_{\rho}$ for a density-operator preparation.

(c) **Momentum observable.** $P_{j}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(P_{j})=\{\psi\in H:\xi_{j}\mathcal F_{2}\psi\in L^{2}\}$ and Fourier representation $\mathcal F_{2}(P_{j}\psi)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{j}\,\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)$; its spectral PVM is $E_{P_{j}}(B)=\mathcal F_{2}^{-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}\mathcal F_{2}$ with $m(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}$, and
$$\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)|^{2}\,d\xi,\qquad m^{-1}(B)=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^{3}:2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}\in B\}.$$
The law is absolutely continuous with density
$$g_{j}(p)=\frac{1}{2\pi\hbar}\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}\bigl|\mathcal F_{2}\psi\bigl(\xi_{\perp},\tfrac{p}{2\pi\hbar}\bigr)\bigr|^{2}d\xi_{\perp}$$
in the momentum variable $p$, and it is atomless; moreover $\sigma(P_{j})=\mathbb R$.

(d) **Exact values.** For every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ one has $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ and $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every preparation, although both observables have spectrum $\mathbb R$: an exact position or momentum value is not an outcome of the model's sharp law, while its finite-resolution readings are the Borel bin probabilities of (a)-(c).

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, on the massive spinless model of P5 and on the cited mathematics. The componentwise extension to the spin-$s$ model is not proved here; no joint statistics of a position and a momentum observable, no dynamics and no apparatus or empirical claim are made. The identification of the operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ with concrete laboratory position and momentum measurements is a tested identification under P7 and is not asserted by this item.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and scalar measures $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). For a unit vector $\psi\in H$ write $\mu^{A}_{\psi}:=\mu^{A}_{T_{\psi,\psi}}$ for the scalar law of the pure state $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b). Then:

(a) **Second moment.** $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2}$ if $\psi\in D(A)$, and the integral equals $+\infty$ if $\psi\notin D(A)$; thus the second moment of the scalar law is finite exactly on $D(A)$.

(b) **Mean.** $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ if and only if $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$; in that case the mean $m(\psi):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)$ is finite and real, and if $\psi\in D(A)$ then $m(\psi)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$.

(c) **Variance.** If $\psi\in D(A)$ and $m:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, then
$$\int_{\mathbb R}(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-m^{2}=\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}\ge0 ;$$
if in addition $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, that is $\psi\in D(A)$ and $A\psi\in D(A)$, then $\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}$.

(d) **States.** Let $\rho$ be a density operator with expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted sum below, a term with $w_n=0$ is defined to be zero before any component integral is evaluated; equivalently, sum only over $n$ with $w_n>0$. This convention also applies to signed component means, which need not exist at zero-weight indices. Then for every Borel function $g\ge0$
$$\int_{\mathbb R}g\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int_{\mathbb R}g\,dE_{A,u_n}\in[0,\infty],$$
so the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then it equals $\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ when $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$. It is finite exactly when every $u_n$ with $w_n>0$ lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$; componentwise domain membership alone does not ensure a finite second moment.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

For every $z,w\in\mathbb C$,

derivations.claim: [The profile is a normalizable $L^{2}$ function] The profile $g_{0}$ is measurable (it is continuous on $|t|>1$ and on $|t|<1$ and bounded near the junction) and nonnegative, and $Z=\int_{-1}^{1}1\,dt+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-3}dt=2+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-3}dt$, where by the block comparison of [F2] with $h(t)=t^{-3}$ the tail satisfies $0<\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-3}dt\le\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-3}<\infty$; hence $0<Z<\infty$ and $g=Z^{-1/2}g_{0}$ is a well-defined element of $L^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ with $\|g\|_{2}^{2}=Z^{-1}Z=1$.

[The first moment is finite and the second is infinite] Using evenness and the explicit form of $g$, $\int_{\mathbb R}|t|\,|g(t)|^{2}dt=Z^{-1}\bigl(\int_{-1}^{1}|t|dt+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t\cdot t^{-3}dt\bigr)=Z^{-1}\bigl(1+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-2}dt\bigr)$, which is finite and at least $Z^{-1}>0$ by the bound $\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-2}dt\le\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-2}<\infty$ of [F2]; and $\int_{\mathbb R}t^{2}|g(t)|^{2}dt=Z^{-1}\bigl(\int_{-1}^{1}t^{2}dt+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{2}\cdot t^{-3}dt\bigr)=Z^{-1}\bigl(\tfrac23+2\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-1}dt\bigr)=+\infty$ because $\int_{1}^{\infty}t^{-1}dt\ge\sum_{k\ge2}k^{-1}=\infty$ by [F2] and [F1].

[The state and its position law] The product $\psi=g\otimes\varphi$ is an element of $H$ with $\|\psi\|^{2}=\|g\|_{2}^{2}\|\varphi\|^{2}=1$ by Tonelli and the normalizations of step 1.1; hence $[\psi]$ is a pure preparation. By [F3] the law of $Q_{1}$ in this preparation has density $|g|^{2}$ on $\mathbb R$ (independent of $\varphi$), so its first and second absolute moments are exactly the integrals computed in step 2.1, and every exact value has probability zero.

[Mean finite, variance infinite] By step 3.1 the position law of the preparation has density $|g|^{2}$, so [F5] applies: the mean $\int t\,d\mu^{Q_{1}}_{\psi}=Z^{-1}\int t|g_{0}(t)|^{2}dt$ vanishes because $t|g_{0}(t)|^{2}$ is odd and integrable by step 2.1, and the mean is finite; the second moment is $+\infty$ by steps 2.1-3.1, so the variance, which is the second moment minus the square of the (zero) mean, does not exist as a finite number. By the criterion [F4] this is exactly the statement $\psi\in D(|Q_{1}|^{1/2})$ but $\psi\notin D(Q_{1})$; the divergence of $\int t^{2}|g|^{2}dt$ is the same as the failure of $x_{1}\psi\in L^{2}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, which is the choice hypothesis of the rank-one calculus [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]. Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space and let
$$T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u\qquad(x\in H)$$
be the rank-one operator calculus of that item. Use the notation of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]] for the unit sphere $S(H)$, the nonzero vectors $H^{\times}$, the ray $[\psi]$, the ray space $R(H)$ and the normalization $\nu$. Then:

(a) For every $\psi\in H^{\times}$ the operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ is a nonzero self-adjoint positive trace-class operator with
$$\|T_{\psi,\psi}\|_1=\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})=\|\psi\|^{2},\qquad T_{\psi,\psi}=\|\psi\|^{2}\,T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},\qquad \langle T_{\psi,\psi}x,x\rangle=|\langle x,\psi\rangle|^{2}\quad(x\in H).$$

(b) For every $u\in S(H)$ the operator $T_{u,u}$ is the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto the one-dimensional linear subspace $\mathbb Cu$; in particular $T_{u,u}\ne0$, $T_{u,u}^{2}=T_{u,u}$ and $T_{u,u}^{*}=T_{u,u}$. Conversely, if $M$ is a one-dimensional linear subspace of $H$ and $u\in S(H)$ satisfies $M=\mathbb Cu$, then the Hilbert orthogonal projection $P_M$ onto $M$ equals $T_{u,u}$. Thus the operators $T_{u,u}$ with $u\in S(H)$ are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range.

(c) For nonzero $\psi,\varphi\in H^{\times}$:
$$T_{\psi,\psi}=T_{\varphi,\varphi}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \|\psi\|=\|\varphi\|\ \text{and}\ [\psi]=[\varphi].$$
In particular, for $u,w\in S(H)$ one has $T_{u,u}=T_{w,w}$ if and only if $w=\zeta u$ for some $\zeta\in U(1)$.

(d) The map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow \mathcal S_1(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
is well defined and injective, and its image is exactly $\{T_{u,u}:u\in S(H)\}$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the spectral suppliers. Let $H$ be the state space assigned to a declared system, let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable of the framework with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and spectrum $\sigma(A)$, and let $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ be the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Then for every preparation $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$:

(a) **Probability measure.** $0\le\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)\le1$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\mathbb R)=1$; for pairwise disjoint Borel sets $B_n$ with union $B$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\sum_n\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B_n)$; and for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ the law is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$. The declared outcome law of the model is therefore a probability measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, not a formal weight attached to eigenvectors.

(b) **Mixtures.** If $\rho=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ is a statistical mixture of preparations with weights $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}(B)$ for every Borel $B$, the series converging absolutely: the outcome law of a mixture is the weighted average of the outcome laws, with classical weights.

(c) **Exact values.** For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ the probability of the exact value $\lambda$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(\{\lambda\}))$; it is zero for every preparation whenever $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it equals the trace weight of the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)$, with $\mu^{A}_{T_{u,u}}(\{\lambda\})=1$ for every unit eigenvector $u$.

(d) **Spectral support.** $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$: outcomes outside the spectrum of the observable have probability zero.

(e) **No density and no discreteness are asserted.** The postulate asserts that $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets and does not assert that it is a density with respect to Lebesgue measure or a finite or countable sum of point masses; the operational object named there is the probability of a declared Borel set, such as a finite-resolution bin, not the value of a density at a point ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] clause (iii)). Which structure a particular pair $(A,\rho)$ exhibits is a property of that pair and is not fixed by the adopted law.

(f) **What is not claimed.** No mean, variance or higher moment is asserted by this item; their existence is conditional and is treated separately. No claim is made about the joint statistics of two or more observables, about the state after the outcome, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome, or about any concrete apparatus. The statement is conditional on P1 and P2 and on the cited mathematics.

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

derivations.claim: [The observable and its spectral measure] $A=E_{1}T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+E_{2}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ is bounded with $\|A\|\le\max\{|E_{1}|,|E_{2}|\}$ and self-adjoint because each $T_{e_{i},e_{i}}$ is self-adjoint by [F1] and $E_{i}\in\mathbb R$; $Ae_{1}=E_{1}e_{1}$ and $Ae_{2}=E_{2}e_{2}$. Define $E'(B):=\mathbf 1_{E_{1}\in B}T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+\mathbf 1_{E_{2}\in B}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$; [F1] gives that each value is an orthogonal projection and that $T_{e_{1},e_{1}}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}=T_{e_{2},e_{2}}T_{e_{1},e_{1}}=0$, while [F2] gives $E'(\mathbb R)=I$; multiplicativity and countable additivity hold because the two-point space $\{E_{1},E_{2}\}$ is finite, and the integral of the identity against $E'$ is $E_{1}T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+E_{2}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}=A$. By uniqueness [F3], $E'$ is the spectral PVM of $A$, so $\sigma(A)=\{E_{1},E_{2}\}$ and clause (i) holds.

[Outcome probabilities] For the unit vector $\psi=c_{1}e_{1}+c_{2}e_{2}$, the identity $T_{e_{i},e_{i}}\psi=\langle\psi,e_{i}\rangle e_{i}=c_{i}e_{i}$ from [F1] gives $E_{A}(B)\psi=\sum_{i:E_{i}\in B}c_{i}e_{i}$, whose norm squared is $\sum_{i:E_{i}\in B}|c_{i}|^{2}$; by [F4] this is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)$, so in particular $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\{E_{i}\})=|c_{i}|^{2}$ and the total mass is $|c_{1}|^{2}+|c_{2}|^{2}=1$. For the mixture, [F4] and linearity of the trace give $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{E_{1}\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho T_{e_{1},e_{1}})=w$ because $\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{1},e_{1}}^{2})=1$ and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{2},e_{2}}T_{e_{1},e_{1}})=0$ by [F1], and similarly $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{E_{2}\})=1-w$; this is clause (ii).

[Moments of the readout] With $p=|c_{1}|^{2}$, $q=|c_{2}|^{2}$, the vector $\psi$ lies in $D(A)=H$, so [F5] applies: the mean is $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle=E_{1}p+E_{2}q$, the second moment is $\|A\psi\|^{2}=E_{1}^{2}p+E_{2}^{2}q$, and the variance is their difference, computed as $E_{1}^{2}p+E_{2}^{2}q-(E_{1}p+E_{2}q)^{2}=p(1-p)E_{1}^{2}+q(1-q)E_{2}^{2}-2pqE_{1}E_{2}=pq(E_{1}-E_{2})^{2}$, using $p+q=1$ and $[F6]$. For the mixture $\rho=wT_{e_{1},e_{1}}+(1-w)T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$, which is a state by [F6], the same identities give mean $wE_{1}+(1-w)E_{2}$ and variance $w(1-w)(E_{1}-E_{2})^{2}$, since the law is the two-point law of (ii) and the moments of a finite two-point law are the displayed sums. All quantities are finite because $A$ is bounded. This is clause (iii).

derivations.claim: [Second moment and mean for a state vector] Let $\psi\in H$ be a unit vector and identify $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ with the finite measure $E_{A,\psi}$. If $\psi\in D(A)$, [F1] and [F2] give $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\|A\psi\|^{2}<\infty$ and $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$; if $\psi\notin D(A)$, then [F1] gives $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\infty$, so the second moment is infinite. In the first case [F5] makes $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ real. This proves (a) and the mean formula of (b).

[Reduction of state moments to pure moments] By [F3], $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\sum_nw_nE_{A,u_n}(B)$ for every Borel $B$. Let $g\ge0$ be Borel, and omit all zero-weight indices as stipulated in (d). For indicators $g=\mathbf 1_B$ the identity $\int g\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int g\,dE_{A,u_n}$ is exactly [F3]; it extends to nonnegative simple $g$ by linearity, and to all nonnegative Borel $g$ by writing $g$ as an increasing pointwise limit of nonnegative simple functions [F4] and applying monotone convergence twice, to the measure $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and to the partial sums of the series. This proves the displayed identity of (d).

[The first moment criterion] By [F2], $\int|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean is finite; conversely if $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ the integral of $|\lambda|$ diverges, so the mean is not a finite real number. Together with step 1.1 this proves (b).

[Variance of a state vector] Let $\psi\in D(A)$ be a unit vector and $m:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, a real number by [F5]. Then $A\psi-m\psi\in H$ and by [F1] applied to $f(\lambda)=\lambda-m$, $\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}=\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,dE_{A,\psi}$. Expanding the square and using [F2] for the integrals of $\lambda^{2}$, $\lambda$ and $1$ gives $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}-2m\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}+m^{2}=\|A\psi\|^{2}-2m^{2}+m^{2}=\|A\psi\|^{2}-m^{2}$.

[The second identity for the variance] If moreover $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, then $A\psi\in D(A)$ and the inner product $\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle$ is defined and equals $\langle A(A\psi),\psi\rangle=\langle A\psi,A\psi\rangle=\|A\psi\|^{2}$ because $A$ is self-adjoint; substituting this into step 2.2 gives $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-m^{2}=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}$, which together with step 2.2 proves (c).

[Moments of a state] All sums in this step run over positive-weight indices, with the zero-term convention of (d). With $g=|\lambda|$ in step 1.2, the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite exactly when $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$; in that case every positive-weight component has finite absolute first moment, and applying the signed version of the identity to the positive and negative parts and subtracting gives $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$, using dominated convergence [F4] for the tail sums. With $g=\lambda^{2}$, step 1.2 and [F2] give $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n$, where $M_n=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$ is $\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $+\infty$ otherwise, and terms of zero weight contribute zero. Since this is a nonnegative series, it is finite exactly when every component of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and the weighted sum of the squared norms is finite; having each positive-weight component in $D(A)$ by itself does not imply convergence of that series.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space
([[def-measurable-space]], [[def-sigma-algebra]]) and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on
$(X,\Sigma)$ is a map

$$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$

such that:

1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a
   bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional
   restriction;
2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$;
3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$;
4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with
   union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm
   to $E(B)x$, that is
   $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$

Clause 4 is **strong countable additivity**. A PVM is called **regular** when
$X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), the
$\sigma$-algebra is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and every one of the finite
positive measures

$$E_x(B):=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,\qquad x\in H,\ B\in\Sigma,$$

is a regular Borel measure ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]). Inner
products are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); this fixed convention is the one
used for every pairing $E_{x,y}(B)=\langle E(B)x,y\rangle$ on this page.

**Well-definedness: the projection clause.** The conditions $P^2=P=P^*$ are
simultaneously meaningful and describe exactly the Hilbert orthogonal
projections, with no hidden finite-dimensional hypothesis. Indeed, for a
bounded $P$ with $P^2=P=P^*$ the range $\operatorname{ran}P$ is a linear
subspace, and for $y=Pw$ one has
$\langle x-Px,y\rangle=\langle P(x-Px),w\rangle=\langle Px-P^2x,w\rangle=0$, so
$x-Px\perp\operatorname{ran}P$; conversely $\langle Pz,Pz\rangle=\langle z,P^*Pz\rangle=\langle z,Pz\rangle=0$
for $z\perp\operatorname{ran}P$, so $z\in\ker P$, while
$\langle z,Px\rangle=\langle Pz,x\rangle=0$ for $z\in\ker P$ gives
$\ker P=(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$
([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Hence
$\operatorname{ran}P=(\ker P)^\perp$ is closed, and the two defining properties
$Px\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $x-Px\in(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ of
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]] show that $P=P_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is
the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace, and conversely every
such $P_M$ is idempotent and self-adjoint by
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]] and
[[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]. Finally $P$ is
contractive: from $\langle Px,x\rangle=\langle Px,Px\rangle=\|Px\|^2$ and
Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|Px\|^2\le\|Px\|\,\|x\|$, so $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ for all $x$,
and $\langle Px,x\rangle=\|Px\|^2\ge0$ is a nonnegative real number.

**Well-definedness: the regularity clause.** For an orthogonal projection value
the pairing $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a nonnegative real number and
$E_x(X)=\langle x,x\rangle=\|x\|^2<+\infty$, so every $E_x$ is a finite
nonnegative set function and the regularity requirement is a meaningful
condition on it; that each $E_x$ is genuinely a countably additive measure of
total mass $\|x\|^2$, and that the polarized pairings $E_{x,y}$ are finite
complex measures, is proved as
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

   $\|\cdot\|_1$-Cauchy sequence in $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ has a limit in

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $D(H)$ be the state space of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]. Write $\mathcal S_1(H)$ for the complex Banach space of trace-class operators on $H$ with the trace norm $\|\cdot\|_1$, and
$$X:=\{\rho\in\mathcal S_1(H):\rho^{*}=\rho\}$$
for the set of self-adjoint trace-class operators, regarded as a real vector space by restricting scalars from $\mathbb C$ to $\mathbb R$ ([[lem-restriction-of-scalars]], [[def-subfield]]). Then:

(a) **Finite mixtures.** $X$ is a closed real-linear subspace of $\mathcal S_1(H)$ and hence a real Banach space, and $D(H)\subseteq X$ is **closed under finite real convex combinations**, that is, it contains with any two of its points the whole real segment between them: for all $\rho,\sigma\in D(H)$ and every real $\lambda\in[0,1]$,
$$\lambda\rho+(1-\lambda)\sigma\in D(H).$$
By induction every finite convex combination $\sum_{j=1}^{n}\lambda_j\rho_j$ with $\rho_j\in D(H)$, real $\lambda_j\ge0$ and $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$ is again an element of $D(H)$.

(b) **Countable mixtures.** Let $(\rho_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\subseteq D(H)$ and let $(w_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be real weights with $w_n\ge0$ and $\sum_{n}w_n=1$. $$\Bigl\|T-\sum_{n<K}w_n\rho_n\Bigr\|_1\longrightarrow0\quad(K\to\infty).$$

derivations.claim: [Contraction and trace bound] By [F1] the operator $TE_A(B)$ is trace class with $\|TE_A(B)\|_1\le\|T\|_1\|E_A(B)\|\le\|T\|_1$, since $E_A(B)$ is an orthogonal projection of norm at most one; [F2] gives $|\Phi_T(B)|=|\operatorname{tr}(TE_A(B))|\le\|TE_A(B)\|_1\le\|T\|_1$.

[Real-linearity and positivity on states] For self-adjoint trace-class $S,T$ and real $a,b$ the operator $aS+bT$ is self-adjoint and trace class, and [F2] gives $\Phi_{aS+bT}(B)=\operatorname{tr}((aS+bT)E_A(B))=a\operatorname{tr}(SE_A(B))+b\operatorname{tr}(TE_A(B))=a\Phi_S(B)+b\Phi_T(B)$; this proves real-linearity. If $\rho$ is a density operator with expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, then [F3] gives $\Phi_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E_A(B)u_n\|^2\ge0$ and $\Phi_\rho(B)\le\sum_nw_n\|u_n\|^2=1$; together with [F3] this makes $\mu^{A}_\rho=\Phi_\rho$ a probability measure.

[Affinity under mixtures] Let $\rho_n$ be density operators and $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, with trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$, a density operator by [F4]. Writing $S_N:=\sum_{n\le N}w_n\rho_n$, [F1] gives $\|S_NE_A(B)-\rho E_A(B)\|_1\le\|S_N-\rho\|_1\|E_A(B)\|\le\|S_N-\rho\|_1\to0$; by [F2] and continuity of the scalar limit, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\lim_N\operatorname{tr}(S_NE_A(B))=\lim_N\sum_{n\le N}w_n\operatorname{tr}(\rho_nE_A(B))=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}(B)$, the series converging absolutely because the finite partial sums of the nonnegative terms are bounded by the limit $\mu^{A}_\rho(B)\le1$.

[Uniform trace-norm continuity] For Borel $B$, $\rho-\sigma$ is self-adjoint and trace class, so step 1.1 gives $|\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)-\mu^{A}_{\sigma}(B)|=|\Phi_{\rho-\sigma}(B)|\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$; taking the supremum over Borel sets yields the displayed bound, and the convergence assertion follows by applying it to $\rho_k-\rho$.

[Conclusion] Step 1.2 proves the bound, real-linearity, positivity and probability-measure clauses of (a); step 2.1 proves the mixture identity (b); step 2.2 proves the uniform bound and continuity (c).
